title: Reproducible kernel & CUDA snapshotting for benchmark repeatability
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Our token/sec and p95 regression alerts have too many false positives due to subtle differences in runtime images, GPU driver versions, and ephemeral runner startup states. This ticket defines a reproducible snapshot and probe flow that captures the minimal set of system artifacts (kernel modules, CUDA toolkit version, pinned runtime image digest, runner config, and probe artifacts) to make load-harness runs comparable across CI, canary clusters, and on-prem lab hardware.

Goals:
- Define a compact snapshot format and capture script that enumerates driver/kernel versions, nvidia-smi output, cuda toolkit version, loaded kernel modules, and container image digests.
- Add a reproducible probe runner that can exercise the same token/sec workload (warmup sequence + steady-state pacing) and emit a deterministic metadata envelope alongside metrics.
- Wire snapshots into our CI benchmark jobs so logs include the snapshot-by-hash and the CI artifacts are retained for 90 days.
- Make regression gates depend on snapshot-equality or clearly scoped tolerance bands when snapshots are not identical.

Success criteria:
1) Every benchmark CI run emits a snapshot file (json.gz) and an immutable reference to the pinned runtime image digest.
2) Nightly and PR benchmark regressions that trigger alerts include the snapshot hash and a suggested root cause hint (e.g., driver change, image digest change).
3) We reduce noise in p95/tokens/sec alerts by at least 30% in the first month after rollout.

Deliverables:
- capture_snapshot.sh (bash) + lightweight protobuf/json schema for snapshot envelope.
- probe-runner v2 image with deterministic startup hooks and labelled kernel/cuda checks.
- CI integration: benchmark job step that uploads snapshot artifact and verifies image digests.
- PRD + runbook entry for when snapshot mismatch explains regression.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We will not attempt to freeze OS patch level; instead we capture kernel version and module list to identify mismatches. Freezing OS would increase infra maintenance cost.
- For on-prem/private customers, snapshots will be stored on their S3/Vault — we provide the schema and tools but not guaranteed upload.

Approach:
1) Prototype capture script that supports AMD/NVIDIA detection, outputs JSON with stable keys, and computes a content-hash.
2) Modify load harness to consume the snapshot envelope and emit the snapshot hash in benchmark metrics and logs.
3) Update the regression gate logic (alerts pipeline) to consult snapshot hash; if hash differs, either suppress alert or escalate with low-confidence tag.
4) Run an analysis sweep across the last 90 days of benchmark runs to identify common causes of snapshot differences and tune tolerance bands.

Risks:
- Some regressions will be caused by subtle kernel driver micro-behavior not captured by our snapshot; mitigate by adding targeted probes (microbenchmarks) if repeated.
- Requiring exact image digests may block routine infra updates; we'll add escalation policy and timeboxed auto-accept for infra automation teams.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (prototype): capture script + small probe runner image, local lab validation.
- Week 2 (integration): CI job change + attach snapshot artifacts to PRs.
- Week 3 (gating): soft-gate in alerts (tagged nonblocking) with monitoring on noise delta.
- Week 4 (enforce): strong-gate where snapshot mismatch suppresses auto-regressions but creates a follow-up ticket for infra review.

Test plan:
- Run probe runner across GPU variants (A100, A5000, V100) and ensure snapshot captures expected fields.
- Synthetic regression test: flip driver version in staging image and verify alert path shows driver as cause.

Notes: This intentionally focuses on capture and visibility rather than heavy-handed blocking so platform teams can adopt incrementally.

2025-02-18 - Miguel Ortega: Prototype capture script pushed to experimental repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-probes/compare/proto-snapshot (WIP). Found discrepancy in how different runtimes populate /proc/driver/nvidia/version.
2025-02-20 - SRE review (Lina Chen): Suggested we capture container runtime (runc/crun), cgroup v1/v2 mode, and OCI runtime config via 'crictl inspect' where available.

2025-02-24 - Performance team (Noah Patel): Ran probe-runner against A100 testbed. Early results: snapshot hash changed when CUDA minor version bumped from 12.1.0 to 12.1.1; probe micro-latency changed ~2.1% — recommend adding 'cuda_patch' field to envelope.
2025-03-01 - PR feedback (Miguel): Updated probe-runner image to embed git commit and image-digest in /etc/bench-info; opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-probes/pull/87
2025-03-02 - Aisha Raman: Updated acceptance criteria to include artifact retention policy (90 days) and success metric (30% noise reduction target).
notes: Prefer JSON snapshot envelope for human-readability; gzip for storage savings.
Snapshot hash must be computed deterministically: sort keys, normalize timestamps to iso8601 without subsecond resolution.
